title: LCEL: the pipe-based composition language
description: The LangChain Expression Language (LCEL) composes runnables with the pipe operator: prompt | model | parser. Everything (prompts, models, retrievers, parsers) is a Runnable with shared invoke/batch/stream/async interfaces. LCEL made chains declarative, composable, and automatically parallelizable.

demo.program:
print('chain = prompt | model | StrOutputParser()')
print('one interface: invoke / batch / stream / astream')
demo.expected_output:
chain = prompt | model | StrOutputParser()
one interface: invoke / batch / stream / astream

title: Prompt templates
description: PromptTemplate and ChatPromptTemplate turn prompts into reusable, variable-filled components with partial application and few-shot support. Templates compose inside LCEL chains like any other runnable. Versioned templates are how prompts stay maintainable as apps grow.

t: Chains: sequences with memory of structure
title: Chains: sequences with memory of structure
description: Chains wire runnables into sequences, maps, and branches; LCEL replaced most classic Chain classes with plain composition. The mental model shifted from framework classes to function composition. Modern LangChain code is mostly pipes, not subclasses.

title: Agents: models that use tools
description: Agents loop: the model reasons, picks a tool, observes the result, and repeats until done. create_react_agent and structured tool definitions (name, description, schema) are the current pattern. Agents turn an LLM from an answerer into a doer.

demo.program: print('agent loop: reason -> act(tool) -> observe -> repeat')
demo.expected_output: agent loop: reason -> act(tool) -> observe -> repeat

title: Tool definitions with schemas
description: Tools are functions with a name, description, and Pydantic arg schema; the model sees the schema and generates valid calls. Good descriptions are the API docs the model reads. Schema-validated tools are what make agents reliable.

title: Memory: conversation state
description: Memory components (ConversationBufferMemory, summaries, entity memory) persist chat state across turns and inject it into prompts. Newer patterns store memory in external stores and summarize to bound context. Memory is what makes multi-turn apps coherent.

title: Retrievers and RAG chains
description: Retrievers fetch relevant documents from vector stores; RAG chains stuff them into prompts with citations. LangChain's document loaders + text splitters + vector store integrations cover the whole ingest path. RAG is LangChain's flagship pattern.

title: Streaming and async everywhere
description: Runnables stream tokens and support async variants, so UIs render progressively and servers handle concurrency. astream_events exposes intermediate steps (tool calls, retriever hits) for rich UIs. Streaming is table stakes for chat products.

title: LangGraph: stateful agent graphs
description: LangGraph models agents as graphs with explicit state, nodes, and edges, adding persistence, human-in-the-loop interrupts, and time travel. It is the answer to 'my agent loop needs control flow.' Complex agents are graphs, not scripts.

title: Callbacks and tracing
description: Callbacks hook token, chain, and tool events for logging and UIs; LangSmith (hosted) traces runs end to end for debugging. Tracing turns 'the agent did something weird' into an inspectable run tree. Observability is built into the runnable protocol.

title: Output parsers
description: Output parsers (StrOutputParser, JsonOutputParser, PydanticOutputParser) convert raw model text into typed values with retry-on-format-error. Structured output is enforced, not hoped for. Parsers are the last mile of reliability.

title: The langchain-core split
description: In 2024 the project split into langchain-core (stable abstractions), langchain (chains/agents), and langchain-community (integrations), so apps pin stable cores while integrations churn. The split signaled maturity: interfaces over implementations. Depend on core, swap the rest.

title: Evaluations with LangSmith
description: LangSmith datasets + evaluators score chains on goldens with LLM or heuristic judges, tracking scores across prompt/model changes. Eval-driven iteration is how prompt changes stop being guesses. The framework and the eval platform are designed together.

title: When to skip the framework
description: For a single prompt call, direct SDK use is simpler; LangChain pays off when chains, tools, memory, or retrieval compose. Framework overhead is real and should be spent deliberately. Use it where composition happens.
